and I got the following error of my first try:

Error in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines,
na.strings, :
scan() expected 'an integer', got 'PROBE_X_POS'
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In fcn(...) : Packages reordered in search path: package:affy
2: In computeAffinities.AffymetrixCdfFile(cdf, paths = probePath,
verbose = less(verbose)) :
NAs introduced by coercion

Which i figured it because the R code is not expecting the header from

bc <- GcRmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)

> verbose = less(verbose)) :

>
> Which i figured it because the R code is not expecting the header from
> the files. So I took off the headers from both files and rerun

Thanks for pointing this out. The format of Affymetrix's NetAffx
files tend to change over time and differ between chip types. We've
tried to make the code clever about these things, but here it fails.
I put it on my todo list to fix this. It is also on the todo list to
have GcRmaBackgroundCorrection utilize *.acs (aroma cell sequence)
binary files instead.

However, since Affymetrix provides two seperate probe_tab for
GenomeWideSNP_6 (same for GenomeWideSNP_5) - one for SNPs and one for
CN probes - GcRmaBackgroundCorrection will not work for these chip
types. This is why we need to move to *.acs files instead.

FYI, the GCRMA method has very low priority from my side. The
algorithm implemented in the gcrma package has showed to change over
time resulting in different results depending on version (an issue
raised several times on the Bioconductor mailing list). Because of
this, I'm personally less interesting in keep supporting it because it
is not stable itself.

FYI 2, we don't have the time/resources to troubleshoot old versions
of packages and/or R. You're running a more than one year old version
of R, which is why you get an old version of gcrma too. If you don't
provide troubleshooting reports for more recent versions, it is quite
likely that we prioritize other things before this.

Cheers,

Henrik
